question: For each of the 23 medium-and-above reviewer findings that the off-contract verdict shape silently dropped, is it (a) already fixed incidentally, (b) still a live defect on current main, or (c) not actually a defect / no longer applicable?
roster_source: Transcribed from task 5430's own description, which is the authoritative enumeration. Each id is <task>-<category>-<corpus index>. 22 of 23 resolve to a live issue record in the frozen corpus/ in this directory; 2896-correctness-0 does not, because that verdict was overwritten by a re-review on 2026-09-12 and its headline survives only in the task description. Severity and category are as emitted, never re-graded here.

roster.headline: Storm-escalation dedup is broken: filed with task_id='' but queried by entity_uuid
report_ready_to_merge is not in the architect's tool allowlist — the exit is unreachable in production
The enqueue exit's 'blocked + no escalation is LEAVE-shaped' rationale is contradicted by the sweep's EXISTS_OFF_MAIN upgrade
Tombstone coverage overclaimed as "every recon path"
New eviction order makes narrative reconstructions single-trim transient
get_statuses tool description grew 959 → 8,328 chars, loading ~2k tokens into every agent session
The ASSIGNED preserve has no staleness bound and --disk-pressure cannot override it — a stuck record exempts a lane from reclaim permanently
filing_dispatch claims about a TASK are adjudicated as terminality, producing false 'mismatch' verdicts on ordinary 'filed task N' narration
PR/issue '#N' references are read as task refs, so 'Merged PR #4521' escalates against an unrelated task
make_commit_probe() runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` synchronously on the event loop, defeating the to_thread wrapper directly below it
Implementation deliberately supersedes two normative PRD Contract rows, but the PRD still states the old ones
Streak escalation is one-shot for a persistent condition
Progress probe ships with no caller anywhere in the repo
Writer and reader resolve the path from different process envs
Narrowing recovered_open silently drops the 'escalation open' badge for insufficient_data / grandfathered / unjudged rows
internal_error in _UNCACHEABLE_ISSUE_KINDS can permanently defeat the memory-evals cache — the failure mode this change rejects elsewhere
Env-recovery gate checks `attempt.test.rc != 0` but not that the TEST leg is the ENV_TRANSIENT source
A TYPE-leg ENV_TRANSIENT now outranks and masks a co-occurring genuine TEST_FAILURE
The registration-time canary is a FINDABILITY probe, not an importability probe — it cannot detect the exact failure mode the task measured
`--setenv=PYTHONPATH=` applies to the ENTIRE transient unit, not just the submit child — the deploy payload now runs with a PYTHONPATH it never had
Documented-but-unfixed capacity marker gap makes the key probe fail misleadingly
Docstring cites a pin test that does not exist; the load-bearing ordering is entirely unpinned
A duplicate-uuid store row is still reported as `bad_manifest` — the exact mis-attribution this change eliminates elsewhere

gate.rationale: STOP is not available. The task authorises stopping only if all five priority findings disposition (a) or (c); three of the five are (b) — 3041-correctness-0, 3075-correctness-0 and 3142-correctness-0 are all still live on current main, one of them reproduced at runtime. Two are (a), both confirmed by hunk/commit rather than by claim. A 3-of-5 live rate among the high/major band is also the opposite of the 'low yield' premise the stop path rests on, so the 18 medium findings are triaged rather than deferred.

dispositions.note: Already fixed, and the fix is confirmed by the hunk rather than accepted from the task description. b57f8c1402 changed `task_id=''` to `task_id=entity_uuid` in maybe_escalate_suppression_storm, which is exactly the key misalignment the finding named. Notably it is an evil-merge: the line is in NEITHER parent's tree (parent1 c267573b73 still has task_id='' with the entity_uuid lookup; parent2 5b51fa970b has no such function at all), so it exists on main solely through that merge's by-hand conflict resolution — consistent with the description's 'fixed by hand'. `git log -S'task_id=entity_uuid' origin/main` finds nothing without -m, which is why the fix is easy to miss. The dedup mechanism was subsequently reworked by 201c9c018b (task 3522): the fold now keys on `dedupe_fingerprint` rather than has_open_l1, and task_id=entity_uuid survives as an unchanged context line, so the write key and the read key agree on both axes today.

dispositions.note: Still live, with both sides of the contradiction quotable verbatim on current main. SIDE A, the enqueue exit in workflow.py: "'blocked' with no escalation is instead LEAVE-shaped, and the merge callback (or the found_on_main reconciler) flips it done once main actually moves." The comment's whole purpose is to justify persisting blocked-with-no-escalation on the grounds that the recovery sweep will leave it alone. SIDE B, harness.py: that shape is upgraded away from LEAVE. The condition is still `action == RecoveryAction.LEAVE and status == 'blocked' and report.live_claimant is None and self._only_merge_remediable(report.open_escalations) and report.branch_state.kind == BranchStateKind.EXISTS_OFF_MAIN` -> `RE_FILE_ESCALATION`, and the surrounding comment confirms the vacuous case the finding relied on: 'an empty list is still True'. So a blocked task with NO escalation whose branch is off main is exactly what gets re-escalated. The two comments cannot both be right, and neither has moved: nothing since 2026-08-01 touched the LEAVE-shaped rationale except a05136c0cb (task 3537 halt-filing), which did not address it. THIS IS THE MILDEST (b) IN THE ROSTER and should be filed as such rather than inflated. The finding said so itself — 'behaviourally this is bounded ... the stranded reaper has the same exposure (pre-existing), so this may be accepted behaviour — but the enqueue-exit comment should say so rather than assert the opposite.' The defect is a load-bearing comment that states the inverse of what the code does, with a real if bounded cost behind it (a burned architect run per sweep, and a second MergeRequest on the same branch once the 30-minute grace lapses). The remedy may legitimately be a comment correction rather than a behaviour change.

dispositions.note: Still live, with the word 'permanently' now false for one of its two paths. Every mechanical fact reproduces verbatim: the Pass-1 record gate preserves unconditionally on ASSIGNED reading only LANE_STATE_RAW and LANE_STATE_TASK_ID; lib_lane_state.sh exports no age field at all, so the gate CANNOT see updated_at even though the record carries it; the gate is still positioned before the --disk-pressure rm branch, deliberately and by documented design; the arg parser still has no --force/--ignore-record/--max-record-age; and _note_released_durable still swallows OSError with 'cache updated (FREE), durable record left as-is'. WHAT CHANGED, and it matters: task 2891 landed two harness passes the July reading predates. _reclaim_terminal_lane_records DOES clear stuck records — but keyed on TERMINAL task status, not record age — so a stuck record whose task is done/cancelled now heals within a tick. _stale_lane_assignment_census is the only code applying an age bound (lane_stale_report_days, default 7) and is REPORT-ONLY by explicit design. So an age bound now exists in the tree and terminates in a digest line, never in a reclaim. TWO PATHS REMAIN LIVE. (1) A record stranded while its task is still pending/in-progress/blocked is skipped by the terminal reclaim by design and only printed by the census; reclaim_victim (the steal/preempt path) routes through the same swallowing write and its victim is typically non-terminal, so this is a real producer. (2) The claim's core ENOSPC scenario survives intact, because the healing pass releases through the SAME _note_released_durable and therefore fails identically while the disk is still full — the self-healing path is blocked by the very condition it would heal, during exactly the window the operator is running reclaim --disk-pressure. One genuine mitigation the July reading predates: the swallowed write is no longer silent, firing an L2 operator escalation at warm_lane_drift_l2_threshold (default 3). It still neither clears the record nor unblocks the gate. Test coverage is the telling gap: the analogous pin EXISTS for the sibling gate — test_warm_lane_gc.sh 'K5: --disk-pressure ALSO honours the live-reference gate' — while Block S (the record gate, S1-S23) contains zero --disk-pressure cases and Block K contains zero record-gate cases.

dispositions.note: Fixed, and fixed more thoroughly than the finding suggested. Task 3442 landed the repair (commits aa5ac9c415, 5e0938c58e, 41803f5b7c, e63803cb72, dec8c9f480) and task 3481 moved verdictBadge out of the JSX into dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/memory_evals_fmt.js, so the finding's cited consumer path is itself stale now. The producer is UNCHANGED — recovered_open is still narrowed to no_alarm and the *_open states are still emitted — but the consumer is no longer three literals: it is a 9-entry PARITY_REFINEMENT table plus a 4-entry PARITY_PLAIN opt-out, and the producer now exports its vocabulary as a closed PARITY_STATES frozenset of 13. The decisive check is the set difference, and it is empty in BOTH directions: every producer state is handled, and there are no dead consumer branches. The exact row the finding named now renders 'insufficient_data - escalation open' with badge warn, which is precisely the behaviour it asked for. The fix went further than the suggestion in two ways: it is enumerated-exhaustive rather than endsWith('_open'), so an unlisted state fails LOUDLY as 'unrecognised parity' / badge bad instead of degrading to muted; and unknown_verdict now reads 'unreadable verdict' / badge bad, distinct from an absent verdict's 'no verdict' / muted, resolving the finding's second sub-claim. One residue is NOT a defect: _parity's docstring still says the change is 'purely additive for existing consumers'. The finding offered a disjunctive remedy — fix the consumer OR drop the claim — and the consumer was fixed, which makes the sentence true rather than misleading. No follow-up is warranted.

dispositions.note: Still live, verbatim. The gate in verify.py still reads `category == FailureCategory.ENV_TRANSIENT and attempt.test.cmd is not None and attempt.test.rc != 0`, and the comment block above it still states THE RULE as 'it therefore fires only when the TEST leg is the failing one' while explicitly resting that on 'an explicit `attempt.test.rc != 0`'. The finding's objection is untouched: rc != 0 establishes only that the test leg failed SOMEHOW, not that it is the leg which classified ENV_TRANSIENT. Re-measured ranks confirm the masking is still possible — ENV_TRANSIENT severity_rank 10 still outranks TEST_FAILURE 11 (the absolute numbers shifted by one since August, the ORDER is identical), so a phantom TYPE-leg ENV_TRANSIENT still sets the aggregate category while a genuine test regression holds rc=1. The comment has in fact acquired a defence that does not reach the finding: 'The rc check is correct on its own terms ... re-running a passing leg can never recover anything.' True, and irrelevant — it answers the rc==0 case, not the rc!=0-for-a-real-regression case the finding describes. The sharpest evidence is thirty lines below the gate: the bare-xdist reclassification guard requires `attempt.test.rc != 0 and attempt.lint.rc == 0 and attempt.type.rc == 0` — precisely the co-occurrence guard this gate lacks, in the same function, added for the same reason. The finding cited that as in-repo precedent; it is still precedent, and still unapplied here.

dispositions.note: Still live, and the remedy is now CHEAPER than when the finding was written. Confirmed by measurement rather than reading: ENV_TRANSIENT is severity_rank 10 and TEST_FAILURE 11, so ENV_TRANSIENT still wins _worst_category; ENV_TRANSIENT is still a member of INFRA_TRANSIENT_CATEGORIES; and merge_queue.py still routes on the AGGREGATE at three sites (`(verify.category or '') in INFRA_TRANSIENT_CATEGORIES`), so a run whose TYPE leg is phantom-red and whose TEST leg is genuinely red is still held as transient infra with no steward and no branch-blaming. WHAT CHANGED IS THE AVAILABILITY OF THE FIX, not the defect. The repo now carries per-leg categories (`local_verify.failing_leg_categories`, pinned by TestSummarizeChecksReportsEveryFailingLegCategory) and has already adopted the exact principle this finding asks for, in a comment headed 'GATE ON EVERY FAILING LEG, NOT THE AGGREGATE CATEGORY (task 3173 review)' — whose reasoning is the same shape as this finding's: severity_rank lets a high-severity infra leg dominate a co-occurring branch-blaming TEST_FAILURE, which is correct for 'how bad was this run' and wrong for attribution. That principle was applied ONLY to the indeterminate-verdict veto cross-check. The infra-transient routing three functions away still keys on the single aggregate value. So the fix no longer needs new machinery — it needs the existing machinery extended to a site that was missed, and the inconsistency between the two adjacent policies is now itself the argument.

dispositions.note: Fixed, and dispositioned the way the finding demanded — by searching for a pin test, not by re-reading the docstring. TestAnchoredSlotTimeoutWithCollateralIsEnvTransient now EXISTS at orchestrator/tests/test_verify_classify.py, and it pins exactly what the docstring claims: the full slot-shape x collateral-shape x order cross-product classifying ENV_TRANSIENT rather than SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT. In August that grep returned nothing repo-wide. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS THE MOST INTERESTING (a) IN THE ROSTER. First, the fixing work is labelled 'task 4126 (recovered from the task-3679 review)' in both the test's comment block and its class docstring — so this finding was independently RECOVERED and acted on through some route other than the review gate that dropped it. It is direct evidence that the dropped-finding population was not uniformly lost, and the only such evidence in this triage. Second, the repo has since grown a structural guard against the whole defect CLASS: orchestrator/tests/test_cited_test_class_drift.py asserts that every test class cited by name in a src docstring actually resolves to a real class, and its module docstring names this very incident as the motivation — 'orchestrator.verify_classify carried one for TEN DAYS naming a class that existed nowhere in the repo (citation landed 2026-08-05; the class was written 2026-08-15)'. The finding's own remedy was one test; what landed was that test plus a detector for every future instance. No follow-up is warranted.
